gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 640 × 512 thermal drones it lists do not resolve the same detail: by DJI's own FOV figures one thermal pixel covers about 10 cm at 100 m on the Matrice 4T against about 14 cm on the Mavic 3T, and the 3 cm-per-pixel figure that FLIR-sourced guidance cites from IEC TS 62446-3 for detailed solar inspection therefore means flying at roughly 30 m and 21 m respectively.
standout_why: Compared against blog.dronetrader.com/thermal-drones-for-sale, bestthermaldrone.com/best-thermal-drones, bestthermaldrone.com/compare and nighthunting.net/thermal-drones. dronetrader gives resolution and prices only, with no focal length, FOV, pixel pitch or range, and already says thermal does not see through glass. bestthermaldrone gives the inputs (9.1 mm and 13 mm Autel lenses, 45° and 61° DJI diagonal FOV, NETD, 30 Hz) but no pixel pitch, no per-pixel footprint and no distance rule. nighthunting shows bare 'mm' values with no range or pixels-on-target figure. None mentions the 3 cm-per-pixel solar rule. The B&H compare pages were not opened, so I cannot say whether they print pixel pitch. Rivals hold part of this (the lens figures); the per-pixel consequence and the flying-height limit are new. Autel's own pixel pitch was not sourced, so for the Autel drones Dealectric lists the finding rests on focal length alone.
decides: ChatGPT told the shopper '640 × 512 is a good target' and showed three drones that all meet it, so resolution cannot separate them; the lens does. Among the Autel drones Dealectric lists, the EVO II Dual 640T V3 (13 mm) has a 1.43× longer thermal lens than the EVO Lite 640T (9.1 mm), so it is the pick for wildlife spotting, search and solar or roof work from height, provided both use the same detector pitch (not sourced for Autel). The EVO Lite 640T at $3,359 stays the pick for close-range work and budget, at $1,040 less than the EVO II Rugged Bundle on autelpilot.com. Autel's US store prints the same 'recognizing subjects at up to 100m' line for both lenses, so the maker's range claim does not separate them.

findings.label: Thermal imager, pixel pitch, lens and frame rate (maker's words)
findings.value: uncooled vanadium oxide (VOx), 640 × 512, pixel pitch 12 μm, DFOV 45°±0.3°, 53 mm equivalent, f/1.0, 30 Hz, 8 μm to 14 μm

findings.note: Maker spec page. 1280 × 1024 output appears only with Super Resolution on and Night Mode off; the detector is 640 × 512.

findings.label: Thermal imager, pixel pitch, lens and frame rate (maker's words)
findings.value: Uncooled VOx Microbolometer, pixel pitch 12 μm, DFOV 61°, 40 mm equivalent, f/1.0, focus 5 m to ∞, 30 Hz, 8-14 μm
findings.source_title: DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise Series - Specs - DJI Enterprise
findings.note: Maker spec page. Same detector resolution and pitch as the Matrice 4T, but a wider lens.

findings.label: Ground covered by one thermal pixel at 100 m (computed from DJI's diagonal FOV)
findings.value: Matrice 4T about 10.1 cm; Mavic 3 Thermal about 14.4 cm
findings.source_title: DJI Matrice 4 Series - Specs - DJI Enterprise
findings.note: My arithmetic, not DJI's. Diagonal of 640 × 512 = 819.6 pixels. Angle per pixel = 2·tan(DFOV/2)/819.6: Matrice 4T 2·tan(22.5°)/819.6 = 1.011 mrad; Mavic 3T 2·tan(30.5°)/819.6 = 1.437 mrad (DFOV 61° from https://enterprise.dji.com/mavic-3-enterprise/specs). Multiply by 100 m. Ignores lens distortion and blur.

findings.label: Geometric resolution asked for detailed solar-panel thermography under IEC TS 62446-3
findings.value: 3 cm per pixel, which gives a five-by-five-pixel square inside each cell; minimum irradiance 600 W/m²
findings.source_title: Thermal Inspection of Solar Panels - Commercial UAV News (contributed guest article, 2022-07-07)
findings.note: Quotes: 'you need to fly at an altitude that would produce a 3 cm-per-pixel ground sample distance on the panels' and 'a five-by-five-pixel square inside of each cell'. This is a secondary source; the IEC text itself is paywalled and was not opened.

findings.label: Second source for the 3 cm/pixel rule, with a working flight height
findings.value: 'The standard requires that you need a maximum Geometric resolution of 3cm/pixel'; Sitemark flies at 35 m for 5 cm/pixel and offers 23 m to meet 3 cm/pixel
findings.note: Solar inspection software vendor; no author or date on the page. The 23 m figure matches what a 12 μm, roughly 9 mm thermal camera gives (0.03 m × 9.1 mm / 0.012 mm = 22.8 m).

findings.label: Flying distance that yields 3 cm per thermal pixel (computed)
findings.value: Matrice 4T about 29.7 m; Mavic 3 Thermal about 20.9 m
findings.source_title: DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise Series - Specs - DJI Enterprise
findings.note: My arithmetic: 0.03 m ÷ angle per pixel (1.011 mrad and 1.437 mrad from the DFOV figures above). Distance is camera to panel, looking straight at it.
